subject: bio
title: Enzymes
subtitle: Enzymes with mechanism-focused explanation and exam-linked examples.
concept: Enzymes are globular proteins that accelerate reactions by lowering activation energy while remaining chemically unchanged overall. Their catalytic action is possible because the active site stabilizes transition states.

Rate behavior reflects both molecular motion and active site interactions. Environmental conditions affect enzyme conformation, so rate changes are often due to structure changes as much as collision effects.
Exam questions require precise language about active site shape, enzyme-substrate complex formation, and how temperature, pH, and inhibitors alter reaction pathways.
